paragraphs: The paper introduces a task for checking whether a natural-language statement holds in a three-dimensional scene. Existing 3D visual question-answering systems generate responses, which can leave room for ambiguity when a decision is required. Scene assertion verification instead demands a binary judgment, making the requested output explicit: accept or reject the assertion based on the scene.

To support this task, the authors create 3DSAV, a diagnostic benchmark containing 22,500 examples across six semantic types. They also propose DualLPSS, a model that routes information through subspaces in two stages. Its design combines scene and language information in a way that accounts for assertion type, while using the scene to focus processing on relevant parts of the assertion.

The experiments report leading performance on 3DSAV and better handling of complex logical assertions than existing 3D question-answering baselines. These findings support evaluating scene understanding through explicit verification, with a model designed around the interaction between assertion meaning and visual evidence.
icml-2026-3d-scene-assertion-verificatio.tldr: The paper introduces binary verification of statements about 3D scenes, a diagnostic benchmark, and a model that improves handling of complex assertions.

paragraphs: The paper studies why reinforcement learning becomes unstable when an agent must choose many continuous action variables. Its Lipschitz Pathway framework separates error amplification into four stages: action representation, sensitivity of the environment, curvature of the value network, and stability of temporal-difference training targets. The analysis describes how amplification at these stages can multiply along the learning process.

The authors identify a mismatch between training on isolated action samples and needing reliable value estimates throughout a continuous action space. Action Manifold Smoothing addresses this by replacing individual training targets with averages over nearby actions sampled in orthogonal directions. This provides local neighborhood supervision while implicitly smoothing the value function, addressing two stages of the proposed pathway together.

On the 38-dimensional Dog Run task, the method enables both TD3 and SAC to exceed 400 reward within one million steps, where the reported baselines fail. The paper also characterizes when constrained value networks and geometric action priors help, tying their usefulness to task structure.
icml-2026-action-manifold-smoothing-a-li.tldr: Action Manifold Smoothing stabilizes high-dimensional control by training value estimates on local action neighborhoods instead of isolated targets.

paragraphs: AGoQ targets the memory and communication costs of distributed language-model training. Reducing numerical precision can save GPU memory, but aggressive compression of activations and gradients can slow convergence or reduce accuracy. The paper addresses both kinds of training data with separate quantization techniques designed to retain useful precision.

For activations, AGoQ assigns bit widths according to layer type and position in the training pipeline. This brings activation storage close to four bits without requiring every layer to use the same precision. For gradients, it combines eight-bit storage with an eight-bit All-Reduce operation that preserves precision during communication between GPUs. The two components address stored training state and the exchange of updates across devices.

Experiments use LLaMA models with 8–32 billion parameters on two clusters containing up to 64 GPUs. Against the named training systems, the authors report memory reductions of up to 52% and training speed improvements of up to 1.34 times. They also report pretraining convergence and comparable downstream accuracy, supporting the practical combination of these compression mechanisms.
icml-2026-agoq-activation-and-gradient-q.tldr: AGoQ combines layer-aware activation compression with eight-bit gradient storage and communication to reduce distributed LLM training costs.

paragraphs: AlphaRouter studies how a small language model and a large language model can share generation one token at a time. Existing routers often learn to imitate the larger model, tying their behavior to its reference generation path. The authors show that combining the two models can produce correct answers even in cases where the larger model alone fails.

The method treats routing as a sequential decision problem and alternates search with policy updates. Collaborative Inference Tree Search explores different sequences of model choices. Tree-Advantage Policy Optimization then uses comparisons between alternative branches to estimate how individual routing decisions contributed to the final result. This addresses the difficulty of learning from a reward that arrives only after a full answer.

The experiments report an improved accuracy–efficiency frontier, meaning the method finds more favorable combinations of answer quality and computational cost. The contribution is therefore broader than avoiding expensive tokens: it uses search to discover productive collaborations and trains a router to reproduce useful decision patterns without dense supervision.
icml-2026-alpharouter-token-level-routin.tldr: AlphaRouter learns token-level collaboration between small and large language models through tree search and reinforcement learning, improving the accuracy–efficiency trade-off.

paragraphs: Bayesian-LoRA addresses confidence errors in fine-tuned language models, especially when limited training data encourages overfitting. A model can produce a confident answer even when its prediction is unreliable. The paper changes the low-rank adaptation itself into a probabilistic representation, giving the adaptation a way to express uncertainty.

The construction draws on sparse Gaussian processes. The authors identify a structural correspondence between LoRA's factorized update and a particular factorized Gaussian-process posterior. Under this view, ordinary LoRA appears as a limiting case in which posterior uncertainty disappears. This connection provides a probabilistic foundation for extending the existing adaptation mechanism.

Across commonsense, language-modeling, and mathematical reasoning evaluations, Bayesian-LoRA improves calibration for models ranging from 7 to 30 billion parameters while retaining competitive accuracy. Reported reductions reach 84% in Expected Calibration Error and 76% in Negative Log-Likelihood, across evaluations including familiar and shifted distributions. The additional cost is approximately 420,000 parameters and 1.2 times standard LoRA's training cost, making uncertainty modeling a relatively compact extension.
icml-2026-bayesian-lora-probabilistic-lo.tldr: Bayesian-LoRA makes low-rank adaptation probabilistic, improving confidence calibration while maintaining competitive accuracy with modest added training cost.

paragraphs: The paper asks whether learning a procedure in one representation helps a language model perform the same procedure in another. It studies structurally equivalent tasks written as code, graphs, or natural language, including planning tasks that require scheduling steps. This setup separates procedural structure from the form in which a user presents it.

The authors find that popular post-training methods applied only to code or graph examples do not reliably transfer to corresponding natural-language tasks. Training only on natural language can also produce inefficient gains. Their solution is a two-stage reinforcement-learning curriculum: first develop the skill using symbolic data, then train on natural-language versions.

This curriculum substantially improves performance across the tested model families and tasks. A trained 1.5-billion-parameter Qwen model closely matches zero-shot GPT-4o on naturalistic planning. The authors interpret successful transfer as a form of generative analogy: adapting learned procedural structure to a different representation. Their analysis suggests that the curriculum encourages this process, rather than establishing it as the only explanation.
icml-2026-can-large-language-models-gene.tldr: A curriculum that trains first on symbolic procedures and then on natural language improves procedural transfer across representations.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes predict functions using a prior that describes their expected values and how values at different locations vary together. Choosing that covariance structure usually requires selecting and combining standard kernel functions. Empirical Gaussian Processes instead learn the prior's mean and covariance from historical observations, allowing the prior to reflect richer patterns found in data.

The authors formulate prior learning from independent datasets as maximum likelihood estimation. They derive an Expectation-Maximization procedure with closed-form updates that accommodates datasets observed at different locations. This matters because historical records need not share the same observation points for the framework to use them together.

The theoretical result states that the resulting model converges to the Gaussian process closest to the data-generating process in KL divergence. That is a statement about the best Gaussian-process approximation, not a claim that every underlying process is Gaussian. Experiments show competitive results in learning-curve extrapolation and time-series forecasting, supporting the usefulness of learned function-level priors in these settings.
icml-2026-empirical-gaussian-processes-f.tldr: Empirical Gaussian Processes learn their mean and covariance from historical datasets, reducing reliance on handcrafted kernels.

paragraphs: A system moving through an environment sees only part of the world at any moment. Objects outside its current view can continue moving, while its own motion changes how remembered locations relate to the next observation. This paper addresses the resulting prediction problem by giving a world model memory that explicitly follows these evolving relationships.

Flow Equivariant World Modeling organizes latent memory around smooth transformations over time. The memory shifts consistently with the system's own movement and with inferred motion of external objects. In practical terms, stored information is transformed as the scene evolves, so knowledge about regions outside the current view remains aligned with the changing world.

The authors demonstrate advantages over diffusion-based, memory-augmented, and recurrent world models on partially observed 2D and 3D video benchmarks. The results support more stable and accurate predictions over long horizons. More broadly, they suggest that a predictive representation benefits from organizing memory according to the temporal structure of its environment, rather than treating remembered observations as temporally fixed information.
icml-2026-flow-equivariant-world-models-.tldr: Flow Equivariant World Models transform memory with self-motion and inferred object motion to improve prediction in partially observed environments.

paragraphs: Millimeter-wave sensing produces measurements that can be sparse, irregularly timed, and contaminated by rapid fluctuations. The paper investigates whether the temporal behavior of spiking neurons can help process these signals efficiently. Its focus is the match between the sensing data's frequency content and the dynamics of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons.

These neurons act as low-pass filters, reducing fast changes while retaining slower variation. The analysis shows why that behavior can help when information needed to distinguish inputs lies in low-to-middle frequencies and noise occupies higher frequencies. From this condition, the authors derive a criterion for choosing the membrane decay factor so the neuron's effective bandwidth matches useful spectral information.

Across four mmWave datasets under a shared evaluation protocol, the method produces a reported average test-accuracy improvement of 6.22% and a 3.64-fold reduction in theoretical energy consumption relative to artificial-neural-network baselines. These results support frequency matching as an explanation and configuration principle for the tested spiking models. The energy comparison concerns theoretical consumption, and the mechanism depends on where discriminative information resides.
icml-2026-frequency-matching-in-spiking-.tldr: Matching spiking-neuron dynamics to useful mmWave signal frequencies improves tested accuracy and theoretical energy efficiency.

paragraphs: Image warping helps Gaussian Splatting reuse information from different views, but uncertain geometry can place that information at the wrong pixels. Such misalignment interferes with correction steps, especially around thin structures and fine visual details. GADA builds on the observation that slightly displaced cues can remain available nearby, even when their initial alignment is inaccurate.

The method introduces iterative refinement with deformable offsets that adjust where visual evidence is gathered. This lets the model recover useful information from neighboring positions. It also learns confidence weights for combining evidence, addressing two weaknesses of standard pipelines: visibility thresholds can discard valid pixels, and simple averaging can mix reliable and unreliable warped views.

The authors report better performance than prior warping-based Gaussian Splatting methods, preservation of high-frequency image quality, and a 2.13-fold improvement in frame rate. The approach matters because it treats local displacement as a recoverable alignment problem. Its refinement and confidence weighting work together to improve how existing visual evidence contributes to the final result.
icml-2026-gada-geometry-aware-deformable.tldr: GADA corrects displaced visual evidence and weights its reliability to improve Gaussian Splatting quality and rendering speed.

paragraphs: People can prefer different outcomes while sharing principles about which behavior is unsafe. This paper asks whether an agent can recover those common safety criteria from crowd preferences and transfer them to new reinforcement-learning tasks. The intended signal is implicit in people's choices, rather than supplied as an explicit safety reward.

The authors first show limitations of directly combining a reward learned from preferences with a downstream task reward. They then introduce Safe Crowd Preference-based RL, a hierarchical method that extracts skills aligned with shared safety criteria. A higher-level policy composes these skills to pursue the downstream objective, making reusable behavior the vehicle for transferring safety information.

Experiments cover safe reinforcement-learning environments and a preliminary language-model-style task with varied user goals and shared safety constraints. The method substantially reduces safety costs without explicit safety rewards, while reaching task performance comparable to oracle methods trained with ground-truth safety signals. These findings support skill-based transfer when preferences contain common safety principles, with the language-model-style evidence remaining preliminary.
icml-2026-implicit-safety-alignment-from.tldr: The method extracts safety-aligned skills from crowd preferences and combines them to reduce safety costs on downstream tasks.

paragraphs: Perturbation datasets record how cells respond when genes are experimentally altered, providing evidence about regulatory relationships. The paper argues that existing graph-discovery and regression approaches do not adequately capture nonlinear biological dynamics, including processes such as cellular differentiation. PerturbODE addresses this by modeling how cell states evolve under interventions.

The framework uses interpretable neural ordinary differential equations to represent cell-state trajectories. Its gene regulatory network is encoded through a feedforward network with one hidden layer, whose structure implicitly groups genes into interpretable co-regulated modules. The model's parameters provide the inferred regulatory graph, linking the dynamics used for prediction to the network being discovered.

The authors demonstrate gene-network inference and perturbation-response prediction on both simulated data and real overexpression datasets. The learned model also enables simulation of genetic interventions not seen during training. The contribution connects two objectives within one framework: identifying regulatory interactions and using those interactions to describe changing cell states. This makes the inferred network part of a dynamical model with downstream predictive use.
icml-2026-interpretable-neural-odes-for-.tldr: PerturbODE uses interpretable neural differential equations to infer gene regulatory networks and predict responses to genetic interventions.

paragraphs: Generative image steganography hides information within images produced through a generative process. Recovering the secret commonly requires a private key or random seed to synchronize reconstruction. KIStego proposes a training-free approach that replaces this external synchronization dependence with redundant structure embedded in image shares.

The method uses structural guidance, downsampling, and halftoning to map secrets into a bipartite representation that produces self-synchronizing shares. Those shares contain discrete structural information that guides reconstruction through measurement posterior sampling. A differentiable approximation of the measurement process allows gradients to steer restoration toward consistency with the sparse binary observations.

The paper describes recovery of continuous-tone detail from those binary observations while mitigating fidelity loss caused by inversion drift. Its central contribution is the connection between discrete structural constraints and generative reconstruction of high-resolution images. The claimed distribution paradigm derives synchronization from the shares themselves. The abstract frames this as substituting structural redundancy for cryptographic secrecy, so its key independence should be understood in that specific design sense.
icml-2026-kistego-key-independent-secure.tldr: KIStego uses self-synchronizing structural image shares to guide high-fidelity reconstruction without an external private key or seed.

paragraphs: L-SR1 aims to combine the efficiency of classical iterative optimization with the adaptability of learned methods. The paper focuses on learned second-order optimization, where information about the shape of an objective helps determine useful update directions. Its design takes inspiration from the classical Symmetric Rank-One method.

The core component, a Projection-Guided Secant Mechanism, produces positive semidefinite preconditioners that reshape optimization updates. During meta-training, it encourages agreement with the quasi-Newton secant relation, which connects changes in gradients to changes in position. This gives the learned optimizer a classical structural guide while allowing it to learn how to construct its preconditioning behavior.

Controlled analytic benchmarks examine stability, transfer across problem dimensions, and the quality of search directions. On monocular human mesh recovery, L-SR1 outperforms both classical and learned optimization-based baselines. The authors report strong generalization with a compact model and without task-specific fine-tuning or annotated data. They present it as a component that can accelerate a broad range of iterative optimization problems by reducing required iterations.
icml-2026-l-sr1-learned-symmetric-rank-o.tldr: L-SR1 learns structured second-order preconditioners that improve optimization and generalize without task-specific fine-tuning.

paragraphs: NeUQI focuses on how low-bit language-model quantization is initialized. Uniform quantization is attractive because mainstream hardware and software support it, but its performance depends on the parameters defining the quantization grid. The paper argues that the conventional Min-Max initialization leaves room for improvement even as quantization methods themselves become more sophisticated.

The method simplifies the joint choice of scale and zero-point. Instead of searching independently over both, it derives the zero-point for a given scale, leaving a scale-only optimization problem. This provides an efficient way to find near-optimal initial parameters while retaining the uniform representation that makes deployment practical.

Experiments across LLaMA and Qwen models, settings, and tasks show consistent improvements over existing methods. When paired with lightweight distillation, NeUQI also outperforms PV-tuning, which the authors describe as substantially more resource-intensive. The findings highlight initialization as a consequential part of compression: better placement of the quantization grid can improve model behavior before more elaborate refinement strategies are considered.
icml-2026-neuqi-near-optimal-uniform-qua.tldr: NeUQI improves low-bit uniform quantization by reducing scale-and-zero-point initialization to an efficient scale-only optimization.

paragraphs: OptMaster addresses two steps in automated optimization: translating practical requirements into mathematical formulations and discovering useful heuristics for difficult problems. Language models show promise in both, but can struggle to connect requirements with effective solutions. The paper combines these activities in a single search framework.

Candidate solutions are organized as nodes in a directed acyclic graph. This structure allows knowledge to move between branches when progress stalls, so different search paths can inform one another. Within each node, independently generated verification code replaces textual self-reflection. Evaluating candidates through deterministic computation is intended to suppress hallucinations and give the search more grounded feedback.

For formulation tasks, the authors report leading accuracy on three challenging benchmarks. For heuristic discovery, they report improvements over the best known circle-packing solutions for 26 and 32 circles, plus a cut value of 9,590 on Gset70 using significantly reduced time and search budgets. These results demonstrate the framework across both mathematical formulation and computational search, with graph organization and executable verification serving complementary roles.
icml-2026-optmaster-a-dag-based-framewor.tldr: OptMaster combines graph-structured candidate search with executable verification to automate optimization formulations and heuristic discovery.

paragraphs: The paper tackles the generation of two-dimensional designs with specified planar symmetries. Enforcing symmetry on an existing continuous representation can be difficult because some group transformations can introduce discontinuities. The goal is to build symmetry into the representation while preserving its continuity.

The authors propose a symmetrization framework for arbitrary planar groups that transforms any continuous two-dimensional representation into a symmetric one. They provide its mathematical formulation and explain how to construct it. They also establish its approximation capability for symmetric functions, addressing whether the representation can express the kinds of symmetric designs it is intended to generate.

The framework is evaluated on pattern design, paper-cutting design, stylized topology design, and a material-design task. The experiments demonstrate effective control of symmetry across these applications. The contribution is a reusable representation-level construction: the same mathematical approach supports several design settings while keeping both the requested symmetry and continuity. This connects the theoretical representation to practical visual and material design examples.
icml-2026-planar-symmetric-pattern-gener.tldr: The paper introduces a framework that imposes arbitrary planar-group symmetry on continuous 2D representations while preserving continuity.

paragraphs: Multimodal federated learning combines knowledge from distributed clients that may hold different kinds of data. In practice, clients can also use different model architectures and have strongly uneven access to modalities. MFedPBA addresses these conditions, which make methods built around matching architectures and balanced modality distributions difficult to apply.

The framework aligns clients at two levels. For internal features, a projection encoder uses contrastive learning and the Gromov-Wasserstein distance to bring heterogeneous representations into alignment. For decisions, it combines naturally aligned logit prototypes using entropy-based weights. These prototypes summarize model outputs, providing a second route for sharing knowledge even when internal feature spaces differ.

The two mechanisms jointly address representation mismatch and collective decision aggregation. Extensive experiments report significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under model heterogeneity and modality imbalance. The findings support treating these as related alignment problems: clients need a way to reconcile their internal representations and a way to combine their predictions. The reported advantage applies to the heterogeneous, imbalanced conditions studied.
icml-2026-prototype-guided-bilateral-ali.tldr: MFedPBA aligns both features and decisions to improve multimodal federated learning across different client architectures and imbalanced modalities.

paragraphs: Time-series models often expect observations at regular intervals, while practical multivariate data can arrive unevenly. Existing solutions either introduce specialized architectures or interpolate observations onto regular grids, potentially adding artificial values that distort temporal behavior. QuITE addresses this mismatch at the input-embedding stage.

The module uses learnable query tokens and a single self-attention layer to aggregate irregular observations into latent representations compatible with existing time-series backbones. This allows established models to receive irregular data without changing their architectures or inventing measurements between observed points. The design locates the adaptation at the interface between raw observations and the model's internal processing.

Across real-world forecasting and classification benchmarks, QuITE consistently improves the tested multivariate time-series models. Reported average relative gains reach 54.7% for forecasting and 15.8% for classification across datasets and architectures. These findings support the authors' diagnosis that conventional input embeddings are a key bottleneck. They also show why a small, reusable embedding module can broaden the usefulness of existing models.
icml-2026-quite-query-based-irregular-ti.tldr: QuITE turns irregular observations into embeddings for existing time-series models without interpolation or backbone changes.

paragraphs: Spiking attention can give excessive weight to neurons that fire frequently, even when their activity is not especially relevant. This density bias is troublesome because sparse spike patterns may contain important information. The paper revisits attention as a comparison between sets of spikes, with the aim of separating meaningful overlap from sheer activity level.

Its DiceFormer architecture uses Spike Dice Attention, a similarity measure based on the Dice coefficient. By normalizing for firing density, the mechanism emphasizes spike co-occurrence. The authors also introduce Lin-SDA, a linearized version intended to improve computational efficiency while retaining performance comparable to the original mechanism.

The main evaluation is in audio, where input spike sparsity varies substantially. On AudioSet-20k, DiceFormer achieves a mean average precision of 0.161 with 54.3 million parameters, outperforming prior spiking-network approaches and narrowing the gap to artificial neural networks. Evaluation on CIFAR-100 additionally examines vision applicability. The results support density normalization as a useful attention-design principle across the tested settings.
icml-2026-rethinking-attention-in-spikin.tldr: DiceFormer normalizes spiking attention for firing density, helping sparse but relevant spike patterns contribute to predictions.

paragraphs: When advertisers delegate bidding to automated agents, they report high-level constraints that influence auction outcomes. A complication is that the same reports can support multiple equilibria. Whether truthful reporting is attractive therefore depends partly on how an advertiser evaluates the range of possible equilibrium outcomes.

An existing incentive-compatibility definition requires the worst truthful outcome to be at least as good as the best outcome obtainable through any misreport. The paper introduces two weaker comparisons. Risk-Averse Auto-bidding Incentive Compatibility compares the worst truthful outcome with the worst outcome under each misreport. Optimistic Auto-bidding Incentive Compatibility instead compares the best truthful outcome with the best outcome under each misreport.

The authors show that the second-price auction satisfies both refined notions. This clarifies its incentive properties for advertisers who assess equilibrium possibilities pessimistically or optimistically. The result preserves the distinction between those perspectives and the stronger earlier requirement: it establishes truthfulness under the two specified comparisons, rather than resolving equilibrium selection through a single universal criterion.
icml-2026-risk-averse-and-optimistic-adv.tldr: Second-price auctions satisfy two relaxed truthfulness criteria that compare equilibrium outcomes from risk-averse or optimistic advertiser perspectives.

paragraphs: RoboFlow4D uses predicted motion in three-dimensional space to guide robotic manipulation. Previous predictive-flow planners often combine multiple submodels, creating computational overhead that limits real-time operation. This paper introduces a lightweight world model that connects perception and planning within an end-to-end framework.

Given visual observations and a textual instruction, the model directly predicts 3D flows across multiple future frames. These flows provide an explicit motion plan that can guide action generation by a general action policy. Flow prediction and action control cooperate at slower and faster rates, respectively, supporting a closed loop from observation through planning to execution.

Experiments in simulation and real-world settings show consistent improvements in manipulation success rates and computational efficiency. The authors also report real-time, resource-efficient operation. The design's significance is that an explicit spatial plan can remain part of the control process without requiring a heavy stack of separate prediction modules. Its integration with general action policies makes flow planning a component that can guide execution within the overall robotic loop.
icml-2026-roboflow4d-a-lightweight-flow-.tldr: RoboFlow4D predicts multi-frame 3D motion from images and instructions to guide efficient, real-time robotic manipulation.

paragraphs: Geometry reasoning requires a model to connect a diagram with symbolic relationships and a sequence of logical steps. The paper addresses limited training data and weak alignment between these forms of information. It introduces GeoCode, a dataset built by synthesizing complex geometry problems from scratch.

The generation pipeline separates symbolic seed construction, grounded instantiation with verification, and diagram rendering through code. This staged process keeps the geometric structure, text, reasoning, and image consistent. The plotting code also becomes a training target: predicting it turns visual understanding into a structured supervised task, giving the model an explicit way to connect a diagram with its construction.

The authors report that GeoCode contains greater structural complexity and reasoning difficulty than existing benchmarks while maintaining mathematical correctness through multiple validation stages. Models trained with GeoCode improve consistently across several geometry benchmarks. These findings support both the synthetic-data pipeline and code prediction as an alignment strategy, linking richer training problems with a more explicit representation of their visual structure.
icml-2026-synthesizing-multimodal-geomet.tldr: GeoCode synthesizes verified geometry problems and uses diagram-code prediction to strengthen visual–symbolic alignment.

paragraphs: VERA-V studies vulnerabilities that arise when vision-language models process text and images together. The authors argue that fixed attack templates and isolated attack examples reveal only a narrow portion of this behavior. Their framework instead models a distribution over paired text–image prompts, aiming to capture how the two modalities interact.

Using variational inference, a lightweight attacker learns to approximate a joint posterior over adversarial prompt pairs. It can then sample diverse examples and provide a distribution-level view of vulnerabilities. The framework combines typography-based cues, diffusion-generated visual signals, and structured distractions that divide model attention. These components are studied as coordinated sources of multimodal pressure on model guardrails.

On HarmBench and HADES, VERA-V consistently outperforms the reported state-of-the-art baselines across open-source and frontier vision-language models. The authors report an attack-success-rate improvement of up to 53.75% over the best baseline on GPT-4o. The findings indicate that probabilistic modeling of paired inputs can expose vulnerabilities beyond those captured by brittle templates or individual attack settings.
icml-2026-vera-v-variational-inference-f.tldr: VERA-V models distributions of coordinated text–image attacks to uncover a broader range of vision-language-model vulnerabilities.

paragraphs: WaterSIC examines how much a dense linear layer can be compressed while controlling changes to its outputs. The paper analyzes this trade-off using information theory, giving a reference limit for the compressed length needed at a given output discrepancy. It shows that GPTQ can have an arbitrarily large gap to that limit.

The proposed algorithm assigns different quantization rates to different columns of the weight matrix, corresponding to different input features. This follows the information-theoretic idea of waterfilling: distribute the available rate unevenly instead of assigning every column the same budget. The authors prove that WaterSIC stays within a rate gap of 0.255 bits from the limit, uniformly across all input-activation covariance matrices.

Experiments on Llama and Qwen models report state-of-the-art performance at quantization rates from one to four bits. The theoretical result concerns compression rate relative to output discrepancy, while the experiments establish usefulness in the tested language models. Together, they support feature-dependent rate allocation as both a principled and practically effective quantization strategy.
icml-2026-watersic-information-theoretic.tldr: WaterSIC allocates different quantization rates across input features and achieves a proven rate gap of at most 0.255 bits from the information-theoretic limit.
